_meanings:
<ab>N.</ab> of a Vedic sage, son of Ajīgarta. [In
 the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa it is related that king Hariśchandra, being childless,
 made a vow that on obtaining a son he would sacrifice him to the god Varuṇa.
 A son was born who was named Rohita, but the king put off the fulfilment
 of the vow under various pretexts. At last Rohita purchased for one hundred
 cows Śunahśepa, the middle son of Ajīgarta as a substitute for himself to be

 offered to Varuṇa. But the boy praised Viṣṇu, Indra, and other deities,
 and escaped death. He was then adopted by Viśvāmitra in his own family
 and called by the name Devarāta.]
